expectations.text: Flags the three new columns added to the reviews table and says this per-review data belongs in its own table keyed by review_id
expectations.evidence: FRAMING: cross-module write → container.reviewRepo, with the side table as a secondary architectural alternative. Blocker 1 is «Модуль `annotations` читає й пише чужу таблицю `reviews`»; its primary prescription keeps the columns exactly where they are and moves the code: «Запис/читання/очищення анотації — теж методи `ReviewRepository` (`setAnnotation` / `getAnnotation` / `clearAnnotation`), бо вони мутують рядок `reviews`». Only then: «Альтернатива, яка розвʼязує вузол архітектурно ... винести анотацію в окрему таблицю-сателіт `review_annotations` (PK = `review_id`, FK → `reviews`, як уже зроблено для `pr_intent` та `pr_brief`) ... Це найчистіший варіант». It reaches the right shape from pattern symmetry, but never objects to the columns living on `reviews` — its main fix ratifies them.

expectations.text: Gives the operational reason for keeping reviews narrow — it is the hottest table and an ALTER rewrites/locks it, killing a run in flight — rather than a generic appeal to normalisation or tidiness
expectations.evidence: Absent. The satellite-table argument is «відповідає патерну, який у схемі вже двічі застосований» plus «`ALTER TABLE reviews` з міграції зникає взагалі» — a tidiness/symmetry argument. No hot table, no rewrite, no lock, no in-flight run. Item 13 calls `reviews_annotated_at_idx` merely «індекс, який лише сповільнює запис».

expectations.text: Flags the new ON DELETE CASCADE foreign keys and says new ones should be RESTRICT, with the owning service deleting children explicitly
expectations.evidence: Only the author_id FK (blocker 3, `schema.excerpt.ts:28-30`): «Має бути `onDelete: 'set null'`: автор зник — анотація лишається, підпис знімається». The two new cascades on `annotation_attachments` (`0043_review_annotations.sql:13-14`) are never mentioned as a problem, and no general rule for new foreign keys is stated anywhere.

expectations.text: Does NOT endorse the cascades or recommend matching the surrounding schema's cascading style — the existing cascades are grandfathered, and consistency is the wrong instinct here
expectations.evidence: Passes vacuously: the review contains no sentence endorsing a cascade and no drift-fix that adds one. Its only ON DELETE recommendation is `set null` for author_id, and the satellite-table reference to pr_intent/pr_brief is about the PK-equals-parent-id shape, not about the delete action. Note this is a non-statement, not a stated position — it never confronts the two new cascades at all.

notes: The most interesting baseline run for the delta question: it independently proposes `review_annotations` keyed by `review_id` and calls it «найчистіший варіант» — but derives it from the pr_intent/pr_brief precedent (verified at db/schema/reviews.ts:48, :75), not from any rule that `reviews` is closed, and its primary recommendation is to move the annotation methods into ReviewRepository with the columns intact. So the shape is guessable; the constraint is not. Cascades reduced to the single author_id FK. All repo claims verified (migrate.ts:29-31, DELETE /reviews/:id at reviews/routes.ts:159, client.ts typing via the schema const, journal idx 17).
